stages.name: Elymian, Sikel and native lands
stages.desc: Towns of the Elymians, Sikels and Sicans; Italic and Sard peoples beyond

stages.name: Independent Greek cities
stages.desc: Self-governing Greek cities, free of both Syracuse and Carthage

stages.name: Syracusan-controlled
stages.desc: Ruled by Syracuse or its tyrants, or bound to them as subjects

stages.name: Carthaginian epikrateia
stages.desc: Carthage's province: Punic ports, Elymian allies and tributary Greek towns

stages.name: Contested
stages.desc: Front line: invaded, besieged or held by mercenary warlords

states.name: Cosenza
timeline: Greek towns of the gulf; Sybaris lies in ruins since 510
The Bruttian league forms, with Consentia its chief town

states.name: Crotone
timeline: Croton, one of the great Greek cities of Italy
Dionysius I seizes Croton
Croton is free again after Dionysius I's death
Agathocles takes Croton
Free again after Agathocles' death

states.name: Catanzaro
timeline: Terina and Skylletion, Greek towns on the isthmus
The Bruttian league overruns the isthmus

states.name: Reggio Calabria
timeline: Rhegion and Locri; Anaxilas of Rhegion is son-in-law of Terillus, who called in Carthage
Dionysius I takes Rhegion after an eleven-month siege and sells its people
Rhegion is freed from Dionysius II
A Campanian garrison, sent by Rome, seizes Rhegion

states.name: Vibo Valentia
timeline: Hipponion, a colony of Locri
Dionysius I destroys Hipponion and gives its land to Locri
Carthage restores Hipponion's exiles to their city
The Bruttians take Hipponion
Agathocles captures Hipponion and builds a harbour
The Bruttians retake Hipponion

states.name: Trapani
timeline: Punic Motya, with the Elymian towns of Segesta and Eryx; Greek Selinus holds the south coast
Hannibal Mago sacks Selinus; the whole west is now Carthage's
Dionysius I besieges Motya and massacres its people
Carthage retakes the west; Lilybaeum replaces Motya as its fortress
Dionysius I's last war: he besieges Lilybaeum and fails
Peace restores the frontier on the Halycus
Timoleon defeats Carthage on the Crimissus, but the west stays Punic
Pyrrhus storms Eryx and besieges Lilybaeum
Lilybaeum holds; Pyrrhus leaves Sicily

states.name: Messina
timeline: Zankle, now Messana, ruled by Anaxilas of Rhegion, Carthage's friend
Himilco sacks Messana on his march to Syracuse
Dionysius resettles Messana and founds Tyndaris
Messana is free as Dionysius II's empire breaks up
Timoleon lands at Tauromenium
Campanian mercenaries, the Mamertines, seize Messana

states.name: Palermo
timeline: Punic Panormus and Solus; Greek Himera is held by Theron of Akragas
Hannibal Mago razes Himera; Thermae is founded for Punic settlers in 407
Himilco's army musters at Panormus for the march on Syracuse
Carthage defeats Dionysius I at Cronium near Panormus
Pyrrhus captures Panormus
Carthage recovers Panormus as Pyrrhus departs

states.name: Agrigento
timeline: Akragas under the tyrant Theron, Gelon's ally, rich on trade with Carthage
Carthage besieges Akragas; its people flee in winter and the city is sacked
By the treaty of 405, Akragas is unwalled and pays tribute to Carthage
After Motya, Akragas breaks free of Carthage and keeps its distance from Dionysius
Peace fixes the frontier on the Halycus; Heraclea Minoa, west of it, is Carthaginian
Timoleon resettles depopulated Akragas
Carthage beats Agathocles at the Himera river near Ecnomus
Peace with Carthage: Agathocles rules the Greek south and east
On Agathocles' death Phintias makes himself tyrant of Akragas

states.name: Caltanissetta
timeline: Gela, home of the Deinomenid tyrants of Syracuse
The tyranny falls; Gela is a free city again
Dionysius I abandons Gela; the treaty makes it tributary to Carthage
Gela joins Dionysius' war and falls under his rule
Dionysius II's empire breaks up; Gela governs itself
Agathocles kills four thousand Geloans as Carthage's army advances
Gela is subject to Agathocles under the peace
Free again after Agathocles' death
Phintias of Akragas razes Gela and moves its people to his new city

states.name: Ragusa
timeline: Camarina, razed by Gelon, its people moved to Syracuse; Sikel towns inland
Gela refounds Camarina as a free city
Camarina is evacuated and made tributary to Carthage
Camarina rejoins Dionysius' war against Carthage
Free after the fall of Dionysius II's empire
Timoleon resettles Camarina
Camarina goes over to Carthage after the Himera river
Subject to Agathocles under the peace
Free again after Agathocles' death

states.name: Syracuse
timeline: Syracuse under Gelon, the strongest Greek city in the west
The Deinomenid tyranny falls; Syracuse becomes a democracy
The Athenian expedition is destroyed before Syracuse
Dionysius I seizes power and fortifies Ortygia
Himilco besieges Syracuse until plague destroys his army
Dionysius rebuilds his empire
Dion overthrows Dionysius II; years of civil war follow
Hicetas and a Carthaginian fleet besiege Syracuse
Timoleon takes Syracuse and restores free government
Agathocles seizes power in a massacre
Carthage besieges Syracuse after the Himera river
Peace: Agathocles keeps Syracuse and the east
Carthage besieges Syracuse by land and sea
Pyrrhus lifts the siege and is hailed king of Sicily

states.name: Catania
timeline: Chalcidian Katane and Naxos, Ionian cities wary of Syracuse
Hieron empties Katane and refounds it as Aetna with his own settlers
The old citizens return; Katane is free again
Dionysius I takes Katane and Naxos and sells their people as slaves
Carthage's fleet crushes the Syracusans off Katane
Dionysius recovers the coast
Katane passes to its own tyrants as Dionysius II's empire breaks up
Timoleon deposes Mamercus of Katane, Carthage's ally
The east wavers as Carthage's army approaches Syracuse
Subject to Agathocles under the peace
Free again after Agathocles' death

states.name: Carbonia-Iglesias
timeline: Sulcis, a Phoenician port, and the silver and lead mines

states.name: Medio Campidano
timeline: Punic farmland of the Campidano plain, Carthage's granary

states.name: Cagliari
timeline: Karalis and Nora, Punic ports of southern Sardinia

states.name: Ogliastra
timeline: Nuragic highlands of eastern Sardinia, outside Carthage's grip

states.name: Enna
timeline: Sikel hill towns: Henna, Morgantina, Agyrium
Ducetius unites the Sikels and founds Palike
Syracuse subdues the Sikel interior after Ducetius' fall
Sikel towns waver as Himilco marches on Syracuse
Peace after the Chrysas leaves the Sikels to Dionysius
The Sikel towns free themselves
The interior is fought over in Agathocles' war
The peace leaves the interior to Agathocles
The Sikel towns govern themselves again

events.title: Hamilcar lands
events.text: A Carthaginian army under Hamilcar lands at Panormus to restore Terillus, the exiled tyrant of Himera.

events.title: Battle of Himera
events.text: Gelon of Syracuse and Theron of Akragas destroy Hamilcar's army; Hamilcar dies, by tradition on a sacrificial pyre.

events.title: Gelon's peace
events.text: Carthage pays two thousand talents; Syracuse builds temples, among them the Athenaion, still standing inside its cathedral.

events.title: Aetna founded
events.text: Hieron I empties Katane and refounds it as Aetna with ten thousand settlers.

events.title: Tyrants fall
events.text: Syracuse expels the last of Gelon's family and becomes a democracy.

events.title: Ducetius' league
events.text: The Sikel leader Ducetius unites the native towns and founds Palike beside a sacred lake.

events.title: Temple of Concord
events.text: Akragas raises a ridge of Doric temples; the Temple of Concord is among the best preserved in the world.

events.title: Segesta calls Athens
events.text: The Elymian city of Segesta asks Athens for help against Selinus, opening the way to the Athenian invasion.

events.title: Athens defeated
events.text: The Athenian expedition is destroyed; seven thousand prisoners are left to die in Syracuse's quarries.

events.title: Selinus sacked
events.text: Hannibal Mago storms Selinus after nine days; thousands are killed or enslaved.

events.title: Himera destroyed
events.text: Hannibal razes Himera and kills three thousand prisoners where his grandfather Hamilcar died.

events.title: Thermae founded
events.text: Carthage founds Thermae near the ruins of Himera.

events.title: Akragas falls
events.text: After an eight-month siege the people of Akragas flee by night; Hannibal dies of plague in the siege camp.

events.title: Dionysius seizes power
events.text: A young officer, Dionysius, makes himself tyrant of Syracuse.

events.title: Gela abandoned
events.text: Dionysius evacuates Gela and Camarina; the peace leaves them tributary to Carthage.

events.title: Walls of Epipolae
events.text: Dionysius walls the plateau above Syracuse, with the Euryalus fortress at its head.

events.title: Siege of Motya
events.text: Dionysius builds a causeway to the island city of Motya and storms it with siege towers and the first catapults.

events.title: Lilybaeum
events.text: Survivors of Motya settle on the cape of Lilybaeum, Carthage's new fortress in the west.

events.title: Messana sacked
events.text: Himilco's army takes and destroys Messana on its march south.

events.title: Battle off Katane
events.text: Mago's fleet crushes the Syracusan navy under Leptines.

events.title: Plague at Syracuse
events.text: Plague strikes Himilco's army in the marshes; Dionysius attacks and Himilco sails away by night.

events.title: Tyndaris founded
events.text: Dionysius settles Greek exiles at Tyndaris on the north coast.

events.title: Peace of the Chrysas
events.text: A standoff near Agyrium ends in a peace leaving the Sikels to Dionysius.

events.title: Rhegion falls
events.text: After eleven months, Dionysius starves Rhegion into surrender and sells its people.

events.title: Hipponion restored
events.text: A Carthaginian fleet returns Hipponion's exiles to their city.

events.title: Battle of Cronium
events.text: Carthage defeats Dionysius near Panormus; his brother Leptines is killed.

events.title: Lilybaeum besieged
events.text: Dionysius' last war against Carthage fails before Lilybaeum; he dies the next year.

events.title: Dion lands
events.text: Dion lands at Heraclea Minoa, in Carthaginian territory, to overthrow Dionysius II.

events.title: Timoleon arrives
events.text: The Corinthian general Timoleon lands at Tauromenium to free the Greek cities.

events.title: Battle of the Crimissus
events.text: Timoleon routs a Carthaginian army crossing a swollen river in a storm; the Sacred Band is cut down.

events.title: Agathocles seizes power
events.text: Agathocles takes Syracuse in a massacre of the oligarchs.

events.title: Battle of the Himera
events.text: Hamilcar defeats Agathocles at the Himera river below Mount Ecnomus; Syracuse is besieged.

events.title: Landing in Africa
events.text: Agathocles slips past the blockade, lands on Cape Bon and burns his own ships.

events.title: White Tunis
events.text: Agathocles defeats the Carthaginian army near Tunis, within sight of Carthage.

events.title: Hamilcar killed
events.text: A night attack on Syracuse fails; the captured Hamilcar is put to death.

events.title: Ophellas betrayed
events.text: Ophellas of Cyrene joins Agathocles with an army and is murdered by his ally.

events.title: Flight from Africa
events.text: Agathocles abandons his army in Africa and escapes to Sicily; his sons are killed.

events.title: Peace on the Halycus
events.text: Carthage keeps the west; Agathocles rules the rest of Greek Sicily.

events.title: King Agathocles
events.text: Agathocles takes the title of king, like Alexander's successors.

events.title: Mamertines take Messana
events.text: After Agathocles' death his Campanian mercenaries seize Messana and call themselves the sons of Mars.

events.title: Pyrrhus arrives
events.text: Pyrrhus of Epirus lands to relieve Syracuse and is hailed king of Sicily.

events.title: Eryx stormed
events.text: Pyrrhus is first over the walls of Eryx, Carthage's mountain fortress.

events.title: Pyrrhus departs
events.text: Lilybaeum holds; Pyrrhus leaves for Italy, losing ships to Carthage in the strait.

chartNote: Share of the area of today's provinces in view (Sicily, Calabria and southern Sardinia), by the power that dominated each. Regions are today's boundaries, and each province often held Greek, Punic and native towns at once: the map shows the dominant one, a simplification. Dates follow Diodorus and are approximate.
